title: five satisfies spellings keep a trusted foreign tag trusted while an as, an annotation, and a satisfies composed with an as all erase the marker and are refused
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary': 'Trusted @throws {never} metadata opts out' of the checked panic case. The metadata lives on a declaration, so whether it applies is decided by which declaration the checker resolves for the callee. `satisfies` does not change that — it checks an expression against a type and yields the expression's own type — while `as` and a type ANNOTATION do: both replace the resolved type with the written one, and a bare `(strings: TemplateStringsArray) => string` carries no marker. WHY THIS CASE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS OF THE SATISFIES SET: it is the only shape where `satisfies` and `as` must give DIFFERENT answers. Every other `satisfies` case in the corpus is satisfied by a backend that treats the two identically — a foreign value stays foreign under either, a local value stays local under either — so a refactor that folded `satisfies` into the cast path would pass all of them. This program is the counter-example: lines 7 to 11 must stay clean and lines 16 to 18 must be refused, and no single treatment of the two operators produces that. THE FIVE CLEAN SPELLINGS ARE PART OF THE EXPECTATION even though they declare nothing, because a `diagnostics` case is matched exactly and no more: a backend that refused any of them would add a diagnostic this expectation does not declare and the case would go red. They are chosen to be the shapes a marker most easily falls out of — `satisfies` nested inside `satisfies`, a parenthesised operand, a `const` that holds the result, and a non-tag CALL of a second trusted export, which is what says the rule is about the resolved declaration and not about tagged templates specifically. WHAT THIS CASE PINS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: three `SMITHERS1504`s at their authored columns and the three `SMITHERS1101`s that follow from them, as a sorted multiset — the two backends emit them in different orders. The `SMITHERS1101`s are declared in full rather than filtered: once the tag is untrusted the function acquires a panic case its explicit `: string` return cannot represent, and that cascade is part of the contract. No `messageContains` is declared: `SMITHERS1504` carries a fixed remediation sentence naming no part of this program, and the fragment the two backends share would be a name for the rule. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the marker-PLACEMENT family — a `@throws {never}` on the same line as the constructor, on the class only, or on a class with an implicit constructor — which is measured identical on both backends but needs a foreign module that does not exist in `conformance/support/`, and this lane does not own that directory. It is recorded in the round-6 corpus report as a case that should follow. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column on line 17 from 111 to 110 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 1a54edd0b4348972d60665f0f2ff175f7c6f1bd014f12924dd398355b7f4bd20 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). Line 17 is the ANNOTATION spelling, the one whose diagnostic sits at the use of the annotated binding rather than at the operator, so its column is the one a rule reporting at the wrong node would move.
